l-001.evidence: The lead has two queries: seq 0 is `unreadable: true` (never captured, no evidence either way), and seq 1 returned `total: 2, returned: 2, truncated: false` — an `authentication failure` for `user.name: root` on `host.name: db-1` at 2026-07-27T09:56:07.000Z from source.ip 172.18.0.16, and an `Accepted password for svc.config-mgmt from 172.18.0.24 port 57018 ssh2` with `event.outcome: success` on `host.name: office-ws-2` at 2026-07-27T09:48:58.698Z. The `baseline` block is the empty list `[]` — no control payload at all, live or dead — so there is nothing against which to judge whether these two rows are distinguishable from routine sshd traffic on db-1/office-ws-2, and both are `_id`-scoped fetches whose document IDs cannot recur in a shifted window. Only a populated control payload for the seq-1 query string over a `window_live: true` comparable window (or, failing that, the recorded seq-0 payload) would settle whether `Accepted password for svc.config-mgmt` and the root pam_unix failure are novel; note also that source.ip/source.address/host.ip/related.ip/agent.ephemeral_id are listed as unstable in this environment and could not have carried the distinction regardless.

l-002.evidence: In `observed` seq 6 the top STATS row is `host.name: db-1, user.name: root, accepted: 0, failed: 96, first_seen 2026-07-27T09:56:07.000Z, last_seen 09:59:12.000Z`, split in seq 3 into two 48-count rows (`auth_method: other` and `auth_method: password`), and seq 4's 126-row event listing shows the interleaved `pam_unix(sshd:auth): authentication failure ... user=root` / `Failed password for root from ... ssh2` pairs at ~2s spacing with no Accepted for root. All three live controls (C-14d, C-21d, C-28d, `window_live: true`) also contain large failure bursts — svc.reports 192/96 failures on web-1, svc.reports 108 on web-2, dev.ethan 108 on jump-box-1 — so burst volume alone is not the distinction; the distinguishing field is `user.name` (and the matching `message` text), which is `root` in the observed window and never `root` in any baseline row, alongside a failure burst on `host.name: db-1`, a host that carries zero failures in every control. `source.ip: 172.18.0.16` is disregarded per environment_notes as an unstable identifier. Seqs 0, 1 and 5 are unreadable and seq 2 is an id-scoped doc fetch with no controls, but they are not needed: seqs 3, 4 and 6 agree, so the lead is `present` and non-heterogeneous.

l-005.evidence: Query seq 13 (`FROM logs-system.auth-* | WHERE source.ip == "172.18.0.16"`, 09:50–10:00) returned row_count 20 in the observed window — every row host.name db-1, host.ip 172.18.0.25, event.outcome failure, messages "Failed password for root from 172.18.0.16 port …" and "pam_unix(sshd:auth): authentication failure … user=root", clustered 09:58:35–09:59:12 — while all three of its controls (C-14d, C-21d, C-28d, each window_live: true) returned row_count 0. The distinction is carried by message/event.outcome/host.name (a repeated root-password failure burst on db-1), not only by the unstable address columns: no baseline payload in this lead contains any failed-root sshd row, and the closest baseline failure (seq 14 C-21d, one "Failed password for svc.reports") is a different user, host and volume; seq 10's alert docs corroborate with two high-severity "v2 cross-tier SSH pivot" signals at 2026-07-27T09:59:11 on db-1 and office-ws-2. Sibling queries disagree, hence heterogeneous: the host.ip-scoped views (seq 12/14, 6 rows of routine dev.dana runuser sessions on office-ws-1) look like the baselines' routine session traffic, and the cmdb lookups (seq 1, 2, 5, 15) are state-only records; seq 0 and 6 are unreadable but are not the queries that decide this.

l-008.evidence: The single query returns two observed rows — accepted=6/failed=0 password auth from 172.18.0.19 (first_seen 2026-07-26T09:47:08.979Z, last_seen 2026-07-26T11:16:41.756Z) and accepted=3/failed=0 password auth from 172.18.0.24 (2026-07-27T09:33:35.791Z to 09:48:58.698Z) — against live controls C-14d (accepted=2376, failed=0, password, 172.18.0.14), C-21d (1584 from 172.18.0.20 and 1280 from 172.18.0.14, both password, failed=0) and C-28d (2601, password, 172.18.0.20). Every surfaced categorical field is baseline-identical: auth_method is "password" in all five baseline rows and both observed rows, and failed=0 everywhere, so there is no failure burst, no publickey/other bucket, and no new outcome class. The only column that separates the observed 172.18.0.24 row from the baseline rows is source.ip, which environment_notes lists as an unstable identifier in this playground (addresses are reassigned in container start order after each lever-up), so it cannot evidence a delta; the lower accepted counts (9 total vs 1280–2601) reflect the shortened data span in the restored capture (first_seen only reaches back to 07-26 in a 7-day window), not added activity. No surfaced field distinguishes the observed rows from baseline.
